claims.text: What the image looks like RWMA in a coronary distribution, thinned scar, ± apical aneurysm/thrombus → prior MI
claims.quote: RWMA in coronary distribution, thinned scar, ± apical aneurysm/thrombus Prior MI

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Regional wall motion: 17-segment model; akinesis/hypokinesis suggests prior MI in a coronary distribution
claims.quote: Regional wall motion - 17-segment model; akinesis/hypokinesis suggests prior MI in coronary distribution.

claims.text: Ventricular aneurysm: a localized bulge in the ventricular wall, USU the LV anterior or apical wall, can occur @ the site of a lrg infarct
claims.quote: A localized bulge in the ventricular wall, usually the left ventricular anterior or apical wall, can occur at the site of a large infarction (3).

claims.text: Aneurysm may be sus w paradoxical precordial mvts, persistent ST-segment elevation on ECG, and a characteristic bulge of the ♡ shadow on CXR; these are ⍉diagnostic, so echo confirms it and checks for thrombus
claims.quote: A ventricular aneurysm may be suspected when paradoxical precordial movements are seen or felt, ECG shows persistent ST-segment elevation, and chest radiograph shows a characteristic bulge of the cardiac shadow. Because these findings are not diagnostic of an aneurysm, echocardiography is performed to confirm the diagnosis and determine whether a thrombus is present.

claims.text: Pseudoaneurysm: incomplete rupture of the free LV wall (often I. or lat), limited by the pericardium; may be lrg, almost always contains a thrombus and often ruptures completely; repaired surgically
claims.quote: Pseudoaneurysm is incomplete rupture of the free left ventricular wall (often inferior or lateral); it is limited by the pericardium (3). Pseudoaneurysms may be large, contributing to heart failure, almost always contain a thrombus, and often rupture completely. They are repaired surgically.

claims.text: Eti Ventricular aneurysms are common, esp w a lrg transmural infarct (USU anterior), and may develop in a few days, wks or months
claims.quote: Ventricular aneurysms are common, especially with a large transmural infarct (usually anterior). Aneurysms may develop in a few days, weeks, or months.

claims.text: Mural thrombus: in a study of acute anterior MI treated w PCI, 3.9% developed an LV mural thrombosis during the hsp
claims.quote: A study of patients with acute anterior MI treated with PCI found that 3.9% developed a left ventricular mural thrombosis during the hospitalization (2).

claims.text: Sx Aneurysms are unlikely to rupture but may lead to recurr ventricular arrhythmias, ↓CO and mural thrombosis w systemic embolism
claims.quote: Aneurysms may develop in a few days, weeks, or months. They are unlikely to rupture but may lead to recurrent ventricular arrhythmias, low cardiac output, and mural thrombosis with systemic embolism.

claims.text: Tx and next step Her chart: anticoagulate if thrombus; revasc assessment
Anticoagulants are considered reasonable for STEMI w aSx confirmed LV mural thrombi, along w a P2Y12 inhibitor
claims.quote: It also is considered reasonable to give anticoagulants to patients with STEMI and asymptomatic confirmed left ventricular mural thrombi, along with a P2Y12 inhibitor (4).

claims.text: Anticoagulation may be considered for STEMI w anterior wall akinesis or dyskinesis, weighing bleed risk given dual antiplatelet therapy and the resulting triple therapy
claims.quote: Anticoagulant therapy may be considered for patients with STEMI and anterior wall akinesis or dyskinesis, but the patient's risk of bleeding must also be evaluated in light of dual antiplatelet therapy and resultant triple therapy should anticoagulation be chosen.

claims.text: Surg excision may be indicated when LV failure or arrhythmia persists; early revasc and probably ACEis during acute MI have ↓the incidence of aneurysm
claims.quote: Surgical excision may be indicated when left ventricular failure or arrhythmia persists. Early revascularization and probably the use of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors during acute myocardial infarction modify left ventricular remodeling and have reduced the incidence of aneurysm.
